candidate.answerReason: The total must be a multiple of 30 and have exactly 12 positive factors. The only smaller positive multiple, 30, has eight factors; 60 has twelve and supports all four specified arrangements. This agrees with choice C.

methods.label: Count the possible row sizes
methods.explanation:
A possible number of students per row must be a positive factor of the total, and every positive factor gives an arrangement with equal rows. Thus twelve different arrangements, with no new one available on June \(13\), means the total has exactly \(12\) positive factors.

The total is divisible by both \(15\) and \(6\), so it must be a multiple of their least common multiple, \(30\). Check the first two positive multiples, \(30\) and \(60\).

The factor pairs of \(30\) are
\[
(1,30),\quad(2,15),\quad(3,10),\quad(5,6).
\]
These give \(8\) positive factors, so \(30\) does not work.

The factor pairs of \(60\) are
\[
(1,60),\quad(2,30),\quad(3,20),
\]
\[
(4,15),\quad(5,12),\quad(6,10).
\]
These lists are complete: for \(30\), the smaller factor is at most \(5\), since \(6\cdot6>30\); for \(60\), it is at most \(7\), since \(8\cdot8>60\). Testing those possible smaller factors gives exactly the pairs listed. Each factor belongs to one pair, and each pair has two different members, so \(60\) has exactly \(12\) positive factors.

For \(60\) students, the first four row sizes can be \(15,60,1,6\), as required, and the other eight factor values fill the remaining eight days. Since \(30\) is the only smaller positive multiple of \(30\), the smallest possible total is \(\boxed{60}\) students, choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
methods.levelReason: The proof uses common multiples and exhaustive factor-pair lists for small numbers. It establishes the minimum without prime-exponent divisor formulas.

candidate.annotationRationale: Factors translate the row arrangements into a finite count. The minimum requires excluding every smaller admissible total and exhibiting an arrangement schedule attaining 60, matching the extremal target. Least common multiple restricts the candidates. The written method enumerates factor pairs and does not use prime factorization or a divisor-count formula.

review.mathematicalCheck: The row sizes correspond exactly to positive factors, so the total needs exactly 12 factors and must be a multiple of 30. The complete factor-pair lists give 8 factors for 30 and 12 for 60. Since 30 is the only smaller positive multiple of 30, and 60 permits the prescribed first four arrangements and eight remaining row sizes, the minimum is 60.
